subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What do the letters CAD stand for?
options: Computer Aided Design
Computer Automated Drawing
Controlled Assembly Design
Computer Aided Distribution
questions.explain: CAD stands for Computer Aided Design, software used to model and develop products digitally.

questions.q: What do the letters CAM stand for?
options: Computer Aided Manufacture
Controlled Automated Machining
Computer Assisted Modelling
Central Assembly Method
questions.explain: CAM stands for Computer Aided Manufacture, where computers control machines such as CNC routers and laser cutters.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the 6 Rs of sustainability?
options: Reinvent
Reduce
Reuse
Recycle
questions.explain: The 6 Rs are Rethink, Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, Repair and Recycle; 'Reinvent' is not among them.

questions.q: In manufacturing, what does the abbreviation JIT stand for?
options: Just-in-time
Joined-in-tolerance
Jobs-in-transit
Just-in-tooling
questions.explain: JIT (just-in-time) is a system where materials arrive as needed, reducing the cost of holding stock.

questions.q: What is a key advantage of a just-in-time (JIT) production system?
options: It reduces the need to store large amounts of stock
It removes the need for any quality control
It guarantees products never have faults
It eliminates the need for skilled workers entirely
questions.explain: JIT lowers storage and warehousing costs because materials and components arrive only when required.

questions.q: What does the abbreviation FMS refer to in industry?
options: Flexible Manufacturing System
Fixed Machine Standard
Fast Moulding Sequence
Finished Material Store
questions.explain: An FMS (Flexible Manufacturing System) can be quickly reconfigured to make different products in response to demand.

questions.q: Which statement best describes a benefit of automation in manufacturing?
options: Consistent, repeatable production with high accuracy
It always creates more manual jobs on the factory floor
It removes all set-up and maintenance costs
It makes small one-off bespoke items cheaper than mass production
questions.explain: Automated machines repeat tasks precisely, giving consistent quality and high output over long runs.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of crowd funding a new product?
options: Raising money from many people online via a platform such as Kickstarter
Taking out a single large bank loan
Selling shares only to company directors
Using government tax relief
questions.explain: Crowd funding raises capital from many individuals, often through online platforms, to finance a venture.

questions.q: What is the main aim of the Fairtrade movement?
options: To ensure producers in developing countries receive a fair, stable price for their goods
To make products as cheap as possible for retailers
To automate farming completely
To reduce the range of products available to consumers
questions.explain: Fairtrade guarantees producers a fair price and better working conditions, supporting ethical trade.

questions.q: A designer wants to test how a plastic casing fits together and make changes before any manufacturing begins. Which tool is most appropriate?
options: CAD software to model and modify the design virtually
A CNC laser cutter to cut final parts
An injection moulding machine
A packaging line
questions.explain: CAD lets designers model, test and edit a design digitally, saving time and material before manufacture.

questions.q: What is meant by 'planned obsolescence'?
options: Designing a product with a deliberately limited useful life so it is replaced sooner
Designing a product to last as long as technically possible
Recycling every component of a product
Making a product from only natural materials
questions.explain: Planned obsolescence deliberately shortens a product's life to encourage repeat purchases, raising sustainability concerns.

questions.q: Which of the following is a finite (non-renewable) resource?
options: Crude oil
Wind
Solar energy
Tidal energy
questions.explain: Crude oil is finite because it cannot be replenished on a human timescale, unlike wind, solar and tidal energy.

questions.q: What does a product's 'carbon footprint' measure?
options: The total greenhouse gas emissions associated with the product
The physical size of the product's packaging
The number of parts in the product
How much the product weighs
questions.explain: A carbon footprint estimates the total greenhouse gases produced across a product's life, often expressed as CO2 equivalent.

questions.q: A company wants to reduce the environmental impact of a product before it is even made. Applying the 6 Rs, which action fits 'Rethink'?
options: Redesigning the product so it uses fewer materials and lasts longer
Sending old products to landfill
Buying more raw materials in bulk
Increasing the amount of packaging
questions.explain: 'Rethink' asks designers to reconsider the whole approach so a product is more sustainable from the start.

questions.q: What is one social impact of increased automation and robotics in factories?
options: Some manual roles are lost while demand grows for skilled technicians to maintain the machines
Every worker is guaranteed a permanent manual job
It has no effect at all on employment
It only affects farming, never manufacturing
questions.explain: Automation can reduce repetitive manual jobs but increases demand for skilled roles such as programming and maintenance.

questions.q: What is a co-operative in business terms?
options: An organisation owned and run jointly by its members, who share the benefits
A company owned entirely by a single investor
A factory with no workers
A government-run tax office
questions.explain: A co-operative is jointly owned and democratically controlled by its members, who share in its profits and decisions.

questions.q: What is the aim of 'inclusive design'?
options: To make products usable by as many people as possible, including those with disabilities
To design only for young, able-bodied users
To make products as expensive as possible
To limit who can buy a product
questions.explain: Inclusive design aims to make products accessible and usable by the widest possible range of people.

questions.q: A phone brand releases a new model each year with only minor changes and stops supplying spare parts for older models. Which concept does this illustrate?
options: Planned obsolescence driven by fashion and consumer trends
Fairtrade sourcing
Lean manufacturing
Standardisation of components
questions.explain: Frequent minor updates and withdrawn support encourage replacement, an example of fashion-led planned obsolescence.

questions.q: What is the main goal of lean manufacturing?
options: To minimise waste of materials, time and effort while maintaining quality
To use the maximum possible amount of raw material
To slow down production deliberately
To increase the number of faulty products
questions.explain: Lean manufacturing focuses on cutting waste in all forms to make production more efficient without losing quality.

questions.q: What is meant by 'standardisation' of components in manufacturing?
options: Using common, consistent parts and sizes across products
Making every single part unique and bespoke
Removing all quality checks
Producing only one product ever
questions.explain: Standardisation uses consistent, interchangeable parts and sizes, cutting costs and simplifying manufacture and repair.

questions.q: Why might a manufacturer choose to use continuous improvement (Kaizen) practices?
options: To make small, ongoing changes that gradually increase efficiency and quality
To make one large change and then never review it
To reduce product quality to save money
To stop workers from suggesting ideas
questions.explain: Continuous improvement relies on frequent small refinements from across the workforce to steadily boost efficiency and quality.

specSource: AQA GCSE Design and Technology (8552) specification; New & Emerging Technologies
